title: feat(core): scroll sync + user-overridable keybindings
body:
## Summary / 摘要

Two related additive APIs on `EditorAPI` plus their electron-demo drivers:

1. **Scroll sync primitives** (`scroll` event, `getScrollInfo()`, `getVisibleRange()`, `scrollPosIntoView()`) — Roadmap #13, host-driven split-view preview.
2. **User-overridable keybindings** (`getKeybindings()`, `setUserKeybindings()`, `keybindingsChange` event) — Roadmap #14, implements the proposal in **companion PR #117**.

Both were built with the same design principle: **core exposes primitives, hosts drive UX**. A working preview panel + keybindings settings panel land in `apps/electron-demo` so the APIs aren't theoretical.

> **Note on PR structure**: This branch was cut from `docs/openspec-customizable-keymap` (the companion PR #117), so the 4 openspec proposal files show up in this PR's diff. If you merge the companion PR first, GitHub will auto-rebase this one and the diff will collapse to just the implementation. Alternatively, feel free to review both together.

## Motivation / 背景与动机

- Roadmap #13 (split-view preview sync scroll, P2) — no way for hosts to observe editor viewport or drive it programmatically
- Roadmap #14 (custom keymap UI, P2) — explicitly blocked on missing register/query API
- OpenSpec change: `add-customizable-keymap-ui` (companion PR #117)

**Approval-gate disclosure**: `openspec/AGENTS.md` states "Do not start implementation until proposal is approved". This PR lands implementation together with the proposal because both were authored within the same 2-day take-home window. I understand this is not the sanctioned flow — if you'd prefer to merge the proposal PR first and revisit this one, please just say so and I'll rebase.

## Changes / 变更内容

### `packages/core`
- `types.ts`: `ScrollInfo`, `KeybindingEntry`, `KeybindingOverride`; `EditorEventMap.scroll` + `keybindingsChange`; 5 new `EditorAPI` methods
- `editor.ts`: rAF-coalesced scrollDOM listener; `Compartment`-wrapped keybinding keymap that reconfigures on `setUserKeybindings()`; hydration emit
- `keymap-registry.ts` (new): normalizes plugin shortcuts + command hotkeys, merges user overrides, detects conflicts (id format: `plugin:<name>/command:<id>` or `plugin:<name>/shortcut:<index>`)
- `README.md`: two new sections — "Scroll & viewport" and "Custom keybindings"

### `apps/electron-demo`
- `preview-panel.ts` (new): HTML preview using `editor.exportHTML()`, no new deps, draggable resizer (min 240px, max 70vw, double-click reset)
- `scroll-sync.ts` (new): two-way sync with a **150ms time-window lock** to swallow echo scroll events (a microtask-scoped flag races with CM6's rAF-coalesced scroll event; the timed lock is coarse but deterministic)
- `keybindings-panel.ts` (new): interactive rebinding UI with capture mode, conflict highlighting, unbind / reset / reset-all
- `app.ts`: 👁 (preview) and ⌨ (keybindings) toolbar buttons

### `docs` / `openspec`
- ROADMAP #13 → `done`, #14 → `in-progress`
- Ticks off Phase 1-4 in the companion proposal's `tasks.md`

## Testing / 测试

- [x] `pnpm test` passes — **36 files / 542 tests (+27 new)**
  - `packages/core/test/scroll-api.test.ts`: **12 tests** covering getScrollInfo shape + destroy behavior, getVisibleRange alignment, scrollPosIntoView align variants (start/center/end/nearest), scroll event rAF coalescing (10 events → 1 emit), destroy no-fire, `off()` removal
  - `packages/core/test/keybindings.test.ts`: **15 tests** covering the 9 spec scenarios + fresh-array semantics + conflict recomputation after override + hydration emit timing + destroy no-fire + a CM6 `KeyboardEvent` integration test that verifies a rebound key actually dispatches through the reconfigured keymap
- [x] `pnpm --filter @floatboat/nexus-core build` succeeds
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean for `core` + `electron-demo`
- [x] Manual electron-demo verification:
  - 👁 toggles preview; drag handle on the left edge resizes; double-click resets to 480px
  - Scroll editor ↔ preview follows in both directions; no jitter loop (150ms lock verified)
  - ⌨ toggles keybindings panel; "Rebind" enters capture mode → new key applied → old key stops dispatching, new key dispatches (verified in the editor)
  - Conflict rows render red with a tooltip listing colliding ids
  - "Reset" per-row + "Reset all" restore defaults

## Compliance / 合规自检

- [x] CLA signed (first-time contributor via CLA bot)
- [x] **AI disclosure**: AI (Claude) was used for (1) generating vitest scaffolding from hand-written test outlines, then reviewed and edited by me; (2) polishing JSDoc / README wording; (3) drafting the openspec markdown structure. Core logic — the `keymap-registry` two-layer merge, `Compartment.reconfigure` wiring, `scroll-sync` 150ms lock design, preview drag-resize interactions — was designed and written manually.
- [x] No new dependencies
- [x] No `dist/` / `dist-electron/` / compiled `.js` / secrets committed
- [x] Did not touch `packages/core/src/live-preview-table.ts` (12 Table Widget rules N/A)

## Checklist / 自检清单

- [x] Title follows Conventional Commits (`feat(core): ...`)
- [x] Public API changes updated `packages/core/README.md` + type exports (`packages/core/src/index.ts`)
- [x] New capability paired with OpenSpec proposal (companion PR #117)
- [x] Aligns with headless / host-drives-UX architecture (see `README.md` project positioning)

+## Context
+
+Keybindings today live in three places (`NexusPlugin.shortcuts[]`, `EditorCommand.hotkey`, the built-in markdown keymap) and are resolved at editor construction. Users can't rebind anything without forking the plugin that owns the shortcut, and hosts can't build an "Obsidian-style hotkey settings" panel because they have no way to enumerate the current bindings or inject overrides.
+
+Roadmap #14 (P2, `docs/ROADMAP.md`) blocks the SDK-level settings UI on "expose keymap register / query API first" — this proposal is that API.
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+
+**Goals**
+- Enumerate every active binding with a stable identifier and its source (which plugin / command / built-in module contributed it).
+- Let hosts apply a user-override layer on top of the plugin defaults without touching plugin code.
+- Emit an event when overrides change so the settings UI can stay in sync.
+- Keep existing plugin authoring model working unchanged when no overrides are set.
+
+**Non-goals**
+- Rendering the settings UI itself (React/Vue components ship in a separate proposal once the core API is stable).
+- Persisting user overrides. The core accepts a snapshot per call; hosts persist wherever they persist the rest of their settings.
+- Chord / multi-step bindings.
+- Command-palette / fuzzy search over bindings (a natural next step, but orthogonal).
+
+## Decisions
+
+**Decision 1: Override layer instead of a mutable registry.**
+Overrides are applied as a merge on top of the immutable "plugin-declared" layer, not by mutating the plugin data. Rationale: plugins may be re-registered (hot reload — Roadmap #11), and treating the plugin layer as immutable keeps that story clean. `setUserKeybindings([])` restores defaults with one call.
+
+Alternatives considered:
+- Mutable registry with `addBinding` / `removeBinding` — flexible but every consumer would need to reason about interleaving. Rejected.
+- Per-plugin override endpoint — locks users to whatever plugins choose to expose. Rejected.
+
+**Decision 2: Stable id is `plugin:name/command:id` (or `plugin:name/shortcut:index` when a plugin declares raw shortcuts without an id).**
+Deterministic, human-readable in a settings UI, and stable across editor recreations. Alternatives (opaque UUIDs, integer indices) either look bad in URLs / settings JSON or drift when plugins are reordered.
+
+**Decision 3: Conflicts are surfaced, not resolved silently.**
+When two entries map to the same key after override merge, both entries carry the other in a `conflicts` array. The dispatch path still needs a winner — we keep the current "last-registered wins" tiebreak because changing it would silently break existing plugins — but the settings UI can now warn the user.
+
+**Decision 4: `getKeybindings()` returns a fresh array each call.**
+Cheap (bindings are tens, not thousands, and the array is a fresh flat map), and it sidesteps the whole "did I mutate cached state?" class of host bugs. If profiling shows this becomes hot for a large plugin set, we can memoize until the next `keybindingsChange`.
+
+## Risks / Trade-offs
+
+- **CM6 keymap recompilation cost on every override change.** Using `Compartment.reconfigure` is the intended path and CM6 handles this cheaply; still worth benchmarking with the full default plugin set before merging. Mitigation: batch multiple overrides into one `setUserKeybindings` call (the API already forces a snapshot rather than incremental adds).
+- **Silent dispatch tiebreak semantics preserved.** Some users may expect "the override wins deterministically" — we do that for the *override* layer but not for plugin-vs-plugin ties. Documented explicitly in the spec.
+- **`id` format is public surface.** Once shipped, changing the id scheme breaks persisted user overrides. Called out in the spec so future refactors don't drift.
+
+## Migration Plan
+
+None — additive change. Existing consumers of `shortcuts` / `commands[].hotkey` see identical behavior when no overrides are set. Plugins that currently rely on collision-by-order will surface as `conflicts` entries but continue to dispatch the same way.
+
+## Open Questions
+
+- Should `getKeybindings()` include the built-in markdown keymap (Enter list continuation, tab indent) as read-only entries, or hide them from override entirely? Leaning **include, mark `override: false`** so the settings UI is honest about what's not rebindable, but flagging for review.
+- How do we surface CodeMirror's platform normalization (`Mod-` → `Cmd-`/`Ctrl-`)? Return the raw declared string and let the UI render; alternate is to return both. Punt to implementation.

+# Change: Add customizable-keymap UI capability
+
+## Why
+
+Nexus currently exposes keyboard shortcuts through three unrelated surfaces: `NexusPlugin.shortcuts[]` (registered at plugin construction), `EditorCommand.hotkey` (bound at command declaration), and `EditorAPI.runShortcut(key)` (dispatch by exact key string). None of them let a **host** discover what keys are bound, rebind them for the current user, or persist those choices — the three prerequisites for a settings panel that says "click a row, press a new key". Roadmap #14 lists this capability as P2 and calls out the missing register / query API as the blocker.
+
+Because the keymap is currently baked in at plugin load, hosts either accept the defaults or fork the plugin to change them. Any consumer building an Obsidian-class settings UI has to reimplement the concept from scratch, and cross-plugin conflicts (two plugins claiming `Mod-k`) are silently resolved by declaration order.
+
+## What Changes
+
+- **ADDED** `EditorAPI.getKeybindings(): KeybindingEntry[]` — returns every currently active keybinding sourced from plugin shortcuts, plugin commands, and the built-in markdown keymap, tagged with source id + origin.
+- **ADDED** `EditorAPI.setUserKeybindings(overrides: KeybindingOverride[]): void` — replaces the user override layer, which is merged on top of plugin-supplied defaults on every dispatch. Same call clears overrides when passed `[]`.
+- **ADDED** `EditorEventMap` entry `keybindingsChange: (entries: KeybindingEntry[]) => void` — fires when overrides are applied, so a settings UI can redraw without polling.
+- **ADDED** capability spec `editor-core` requirement "User-overridable keybindings" — describes discovery, override merge, conflict resolution, and persistence contract.
+- **ADDED** `KeybindingEntry` and `KeybindingOverride` type exports.
+
+**Non-goals of this proposal**
+- A React/Vue settings component. The SDK bindings will land in a follow-up once the core API is stable.
+- Persistence of user overrides. Storage is host-side — the API only accepts a snapshot; hosts wire whatever store they use for other settings.
+- Chord / multi-step bindings. CM6 supports them but they add UX surface (partial-match state, timeout) that shouldn't gate the core discovery/override work.
+
+## Impact
+
+- Affected specs: `editor-core` (ADDED requirement)
+- Affected code:
+  - `packages/core/src/types.ts` — `KeybindingEntry`, `KeybindingOverride`, `EditorEventMap.keybindingsChange`, three `EditorAPI` additions
+  - `packages/core/src/editor.ts` — new override layer that sits between plugin shortcut/command registration and CM6's keymap compilation; emitter wiring
+  - `packages/core/src/index.ts` — type re-exports
+- **No breaking changes.** Existing plugin `shortcuts[]` / `commands[].hotkey` semantics unchanged when no overrides are set. `runShortcut(key)` continues to accept the raw key string.
+- No new runtime dependencies.

+# Editor Core Spec
+
+## ADDED Requirements
+
+### Requirement: User-overridable keybindings
+
+`EditorAPI` SHALL expose a discovery + override API for keybindings so hosts can build a settings UI that lets users rebind any plugin-declared shortcut or command hotkey without touching plugin source.
+
+The API operates as a **two-layer merge**:
+
+1. **Default layer** — every `NexusPlugin.shortcuts[]` entry and every `EditorCommand` with a `hotkey`, collected at `createEditor()` time and treated as immutable for the lifetime of the editor instance.
+2. **User override layer** — replaced wholesale by `setUserKeybindings(overrides)`. Each override references a binding by its stable `id` (format: `plugin:<name>/command:<commandId>` for commands, `plugin:<name>/shortcut:<index>` for anonymous plugin shortcuts, `builtin:<module>/<name>` for built-in keymap entries), and either:
+   - specifies a new `key` string (rebound), or
+   - specifies `key: null` (unbound).
+
+`getKeybindings()` SHALL return the merged view — every default entry, with its `key` field showing the override if one exists, and the untouched default in a `defaultKey` field. Two entries that resolve to the same `key` after merge SHALL both list each other in a `conflicts` array on the returned entries.
+
+`keybindingsChange` SHALL fire once on `createEditor` completion (initial hydration) and once per `setUserKeybindings()` call — never per-entry.
+
+#### Scenario: getKeybindings enumerates every plugin shortcut and command hotkey
+- **WHEN** an editor is created with a plugin declaring one `shortcuts` entry and two `commands` (one with `hotkey`, one without)
+- **THEN** `getKeybindings()` SHALL return two entries: one for the shortcut, one for the hotkey-bearing command
+- **AND** the command without a hotkey SHALL be absent from the returned list
+
+#### Scenario: getKeybindings tags each entry with a stable, source-bearing id
+- **WHEN** a plugin named `test` declares a command `heading` with `hotkey: "Mod-1"` and an anonymous shortcut at index 0
+- **THEN** `getKeybindings()` SHALL return an entry with `id: "plugin:test/command:heading"` for the command
+- **AND** an entry with `id: "plugin:test/shortcut:0"` for the shortcut
+
+#### Scenario: setUserKeybindings rebinds a command hotkey
+- **WHEN** a plugin declares a command `heading` with `hotkey: "Mod-1"` and `setUserKeybindings([{ id: "plugin:test/command:heading", key: "Mod-h" }])` is called
+- **THEN** pressing `Mod-h` SHALL invoke the command's `run` handler
+- **AND** pressing `Mod-1` SHALL NOT invoke the command
+- **AND** `getKeybindings()` SHALL return the entry with `key: "Mod-h"` and `defaultKey: "Mod-1"`
+
+#### Scenario: setUserKeybindings with key: null unbinds
+- **WHEN** `setUserKeybindings([{ id: "plugin:test/command:heading", key: null }])` is called
+- **THEN** pressing the original key SHALL NOT invoke the command
+- **AND** `getKeybindings()` SHALL return the entry with `key: null` and `defaultKey: "Mod-1"`
+
+#### Scenario: setUserKeybindings with an empty array restores defaults
+- **WHEN** overrides have been applied and `setUserKeybindings([])` is called
+- **THEN** every entry SHALL revert to its `defaultKey`
+- **AND** `keybindingsChange` SHALL fire exactly once for this call
+
+#### Scenario: keybindingsChange fires once per setUserKeybindings call
+- **WHEN** `setUserKeybindings([{ ... }, { ... }, { ... }])` is called with three overrides in one call
+- **THEN** the `keybindingsChange` handler SHALL be invoked exactly once
+- **AND** its payload SHALL include all three applied overrides in one merged snapshot
+
+#### Scenario: Conflicts are surfaced on both sides
+- **WHEN** two entries both resolve to `Mod-k` after override merge
+- **THEN** `getKeybindings()` SHALL return each entry with a `conflicts` array containing the id of the other
+- **AND** the `conflicts` array SHALL be empty for every entry that has no collision
+
+#### Scenario: Unknown override id is ignored, not thrown
+- **WHEN** `setUserKeybindings([{ id: "plugin:does-not-exist/command:x", key: "Mod-k" }])` is called
+- **THEN** the call SHALL succeed without throwing
+- **AND** `getKeybindings()` SHALL NOT invent an entry for the unknown id
+- **AND** `keybindingsChange` SHALL still fire once (semantic: "the override snapshot was applied", even if partially inert)
+
+#### Scenario: Initial keybindingsChange fires on editor creation
+- **WHEN** an editor is created with plugins that declare shortcuts/hotkeys, and a `keybindingsChange` handler is registered before any `setUserKeybindings` call
+- **THEN** the handler SHALL be invoked at least once during initial hydration with the default snapshot

@@ -71,6 +71,76 @@ editor.on("selectionChange", ({ anchor, head, ranges, mainIndex }) => {
 
 Multiple ranges in `setSelections` require `multiCursor: true` — without the flag CodeMirror collapses the selection to its main range.
 
+### Scroll & viewport
+
+Primitives for hosts that render a split-view Markdown preview and need to keep it aligned with the editor's viewport (roadmap #13). The core does not ship a preview panel — it exposes the coordinates and events a host needs to build one.
+
+```ts
+// Snapshot of the current scroll state: raw pixels + the document offsets
+// at the top and bottom edges of the viewport.
+const { scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight, topPos, bottomPos } =
+  editor.getScrollInfo();
+
+// Sugar for "what document range is on screen right now?"
+const { from, to } = editor.getVisibleRange();
+
+// Scroll a document offset into the viewport. `align` follows CM6's
+// `EditorView.scrollIntoView` semantics ("nearest" is the default and only
+// scrolls if the target is off-screen).
+editor.scrollPosIntoView(pos, { align: "center" });
+
+// Fires on every scroll of the editor's scroll container, coalesced to at
+// most once per animation frame so preview panels don't have to debounce.
+editor.on("scroll", (info) => {
+  const line = editor.getDocument().slice(0, info.topPos).split("\n").length;
+  previewPanel.scrollToLine(line);
+});
+```
+
+Typical split-view pattern: on `scroll`, use `topPos` to find the top-line anchor and scroll the preview to the matching rendered element. When the preview scrolls the other direction, resolve the top preview element back to a source offset and call `scrollPosIntoView` — guard against re-entry with a small `syncing` flag so the two panels don't chase each other's events.
+
+### Custom keybindings
+
+Every plugin-declared shortcut (`NexusPlugin.shortcuts[]`) and command hotkey (`EditorCommand.hotkey`) can be enumerated and rebound at runtime — enough for a host to build an Obsidian-style hotkey settings panel without touching plugin source.
+
+```ts
+// List every active binding with source tagging.
+const entries = editor.getKeybindings();
+for (const e of entries) {
+  console.log(e.id, "→", e.key, `(default: ${e.defaultKey})`);
+}
+// plugin:toolbar/command:bold → Mod-b (default: Mod-b)
+// plugin:toolbar/command:italic → Mod-i (default: Mod-i)
+// ...
+
+// Rebind a command; the default key stops working, the new key dispatches.
+editor.setUserKeybindings([
+  { id: "plugin:toolbar/command:bold", key: "Mod-Shift-b" },
+]);
+
+// Unbind — the entry stays in `getKeybindings()` but its `key` becomes null.
+editor.setUserKeybindings([
+  { id: "plugin:toolbar/command:bold", key: null },
+]);
+
+// Restore all defaults.
+editor.setUserKeybindings([]);
+
+// React to changes (fires once on hydration + once per setUserKeybindings call).
+editor.on("keybindingsChange", (entries) => {
+  const clashing = entries.filter((e) => e.conflicts.length > 0);
+  if (clashing.length) console.warn("Colliding bindings:", clashing);
+});
+```
+
+**Contract notes**
+
+- `setUserKeybindings` is **snapshot-replace**, not merge — pass every override you want active. `[]` restores every entry to `defaultKey`.
+- Unknown ids in the overrides array are silently ignored (settings UIs can safely persist ids for plugins that later disappear).
+- Two entries resolving to the same key after override merge get each other's id in a `conflicts` array. Dispatch still follows CodeMirror's "last-registered wins" order — the array is for surfacing warnings, not for auto-resolution.
+- Built-in editor keymaps (Enter list continuation, tab indent) are **not** included in this surface yet. Only plugin-declared bindings are rebindable. See `docs/ROADMAP.md` #14.
+- The core does not persist overrides. Hosts call `setUserKeybindings()` on every `createEditor()` if they want the previous session's overrides.
+
